quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in blind spots or be missed in a quick glance. Always look for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters while driving.

questions.question: To safely enter highway traffic, you need at least:

options.text: A two-second gap.
A three-second gap.
A four-second gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-second gap.
questions.explanation: A four-second opening gives you and the driver behind you each a safe two-second distance when you merge into traffic.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch for them near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Children on bicycles may suddenly ride onto the road.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space between you and the vehicle you just passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is safe.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you are doing.

questions.question: When driving on ice or snow, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close to other vehicles to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use a low gear before going downhill on slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. Follow farther behind other vehicles and avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes only if you do not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when necessary to avoid collisions. Do not use it to make slow drivers go faster or to get them out of your way.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic soon.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to possible hazards. This sign warns you that a side road will cross ahead.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and sound to wake up drivers who are leaving the travel lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and sound to wake up drivers who are leaving the travel lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn tired or distracted drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means drivers can pass when it is safe. Make sure there is no oncoming traffic before passing.

questions.question: When a child on a bicycle is near your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to control the bicycle perfectly.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles often make sudden changes in direction. Young cyclists can be unpredictable. Children and bicycles are small and easy to miss, so stay alert.

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead to pick up or drop off children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled in before you go. Even after the bus starts moving, do not proceed until you are sure no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: Looking far ahead on the highway helps you:

options.text: Keep up with traffic.
Avoid sudden braking or turning.
Spot police officers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Look ahead so you can plan ahead and avoid sudden stops or lane changes. This makes driving safer, saves fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: In a work zone:

options.text: You do not need to obey traffic signs.
Traffic patterns stay the same.
Traffic patterns can change every day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic patterns can change every day.
questions.explanation: Stay alert to work zone signs at all times. Traffic patterns in work zones can shift daily. Lanes may move or close, so pay attention to signs.

questions.question: To pass safely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. They may seem slower than they actually are. Only pass if you are sure you have enough space to change lanes safely. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift to neutral as you drive through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are the safest for driving.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down, look for traffic crossing, and go ahead with caution.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what should you do?

options.text: Get ready to stop. A railroad crossing is ahead.
You will always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop. A railroad crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Look and listen carefully. Slow down and be ready to stop. Do not cross until you are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these particles and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when a traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do it safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do it safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Try to stop safely at a yellow light. If you cannot stop safely, cross carefully.

questions.question: What can happen if your car's suspension is bad?

options.text: You lose control of the vehicle.
Your brakes squeal.
Your steering becomes loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your car and provides a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beams. If the fog is too thick to see through, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.
